reported.source: owner message in the scanner development conversation
reported.verbatim: 16.08, 25.98 are the two top steps in the "step" area of the object - that's object bottom to top of step - not only the step's height above object bottom

datum_interpretation.endpoint: top of each of the two highest staircase treads
datum_interpretation.basis: The owner's explicit object-bottom-to-step-top description and identification of the two top steps in the staircase area.
datum_interpretation.not_reference: upper surface of the printed base
datum_interpretation.not_feature: the separate broad plateau surrounding the pocket

instrument.note: Two displayed decimal places do not establish instrument resolution or accuracy. One reading per height was supplied.

cad_identity_sources.role: Maps STEP_10 to z=16 and STEP_20 to z=26; names encode nominal heights above the z=6 base top.
Nominal geometry and surface identity only, not physical reference truth.

highest_minus_second_highest_tread_mm.status: provisional arithmetic difference, not an independently repeated step measurement or certified plane spacing
assumptions: Both readings refer to a common underside datum and comparable height direction.
Local tread and underside shape at the caliper contacts correspond to the later scanned patches.

use_constraints: Preserve the original print record and its predeclared CAD adjustment unchanged.
Do not subtract the nominal 6 mm base thickness to invent measured above-base heights.
Do not use 16.08 mm as the physical base-to-pocket-plateau separation; it names a different surface pair and datum.
Do not treat the hidden underside or turntable plane as observed contact truth without a justified datum transfer.
A two-visible-tread comparison can use the provisional 9.90 mm difference without observing the underside, subject to the physical-reference assumptions above.
No new scanner result, accuracy pass, rescaling, calibration coefficient or new print follows from recording these readings.
